_what: CAPABILITY QUESTIONS section (design doc §2 CAPABILITY QUESTIONS, §4.2 row 20): the heading, the three ledger column headers, the 5-to-10 'you ask / what your system tells us / how far we get' rows, and the band-3 hook. Eyebrow 'LIVE, on your system' stays in the partial as template-constant.
heading_html: What we can settle about your AC right now

rows.ask: Why is my AC running but still blowing warm?
rows.tells: Your thermostat, airflow, outdoor unit, ice and timing rule branches out one by one.

rows.ask: Is it just my thermostat or fan setting?
rows.tells: One photo of your display settles mode, set point, room temperature and fan.

rows.ask: Does my filter actually matter here?
rows.tells: Weighed against your airflow and ice, instead of blamed by default.

rows.ask: There is ice on my line. What now?
rows.tells: Ice changes your immediate next step, and we tell you that step first.

rows.ask: Is my outdoor unit part of this?
rows.tells: A safe photo or short video shows whether your fan is turning, and how it sounds.

rows.ask: Can you read my model from a photo?
rows.tells: Yes. Your label fills in make, model and capacity without typing.
Your evidence changes how likely it is. Confirming it needs an electrical measurement.
We organise the clues. Pressures cannot be measured down a phone line.

rows.ask: What do I send a provider before they come?
rows.tells: Your packet: the problem, your equipment, your photos, what is ruled out, what is left.

band_hook_html: A few minutes on your actual system can be more useful than hours of generic troubleshooting.
